target.title: fix(compaction): preserve source message timestamps in synthetic merge messages during multi-stage summarization
target.body:
Fixes #100636.

## What Problem This Solves

In `summarizeInStages()` (`src/agents/compaction.ts#L389-393`), synthetic merge messages for multi-stage summarization all received `timestamp: Date.now()`, stripping the original chronological ordering of the source chunks. The LLM merger could not distinguish which summary chunk represents older vs newer history, leading to degraded final summary quality.

## Why This Change Was Made

Changed the synthetic `AgentMessage` construction to use the earliest message timestamp from each source chunk (`plan.chunks[idx][0].timestamp`) instead of `Date.now()`. Falls back to the last message timestamp in the chunk, then `Date.now()`, ensuring chronological ordering metadata is preserved.

## User Impact

Multi-stage compaction summaries now preserve relative time ordering from the original conversation. The LLM merger can correctly identify older vs newer context, improving summary quality for long sessions that require chunked summarization.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Synthetic merge messages in `summarizeInStages` drop source message timestamps via `Date.now()`.

**Real environment tested**: Node 24.13.1, Linux x86_64, commit 88255cf581.

**Codex review (current head 88255cf581)**:
```
$ codex review --base upstream/main
The change replaces a static Date.now() timestamp with timestamps derived
from the original chunk messages, preserving chronological ordering for the
LLM merger. The fallback chain handles edge cases (empty/null chunks,
missing first-message timestamp) safely. The import reordering is cosmetic
and harmless.
```

**Regression tests (current head 88255cf581)**:
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/compaction.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
```

**Edge case coverage**:
- Empty chunk (`plan.chunks[idx]` is undefined): falls through `?.` to `?? Date.now()`
- Chunk with no timestamp on first message: falls through to last message timestamp
- No timestamps on any chunk message: final fallback `?? Date.now()`

**Observed result after fix**: Each synthetic merge message carries a timestamp that reflects the chronological position of its source chunk within the conversation, allowing the LLM merger to distinguish older from newer history.

**What was not tested**: Full end-to-end multi-stage compaction via a live gateway with a real provider call (requires configured model + accumulated session).

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/compaction.test.ts --run` — 17 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/compaction-planning.test.ts --run` — 109 passed
- `codex review --base upstream/main` — clean, no structural warnings

## Root Cause

In `summarizeInStages()` (`src/agents/compaction.ts#L389-393`), `partialSummaries.map()` creates synthetic `AgentMessage` items for the merger LLM pass. Every item receives `timestamp: Date.now()`, which generates the same current timestamp for all chunks regardless of their original position in the conversation. Only `plan.mode === "single"` paths avoid this by not synthesizing merge messages. When the plan splits (`plan.mode === "split"`), the original message timestamps exist in `plan.chunks[idx][*].timestamp` but are discarded during the `.map()` call, causing the LLM merger to lose chronological context for ranking older vs newer history.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Model used**: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context)
